answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by tying each identity to one licensed walnut grove, where the trees grow along a ferrous trellis inspected each season by an independent warden. The warden weighs the harvest and stamps the yield to that identity, and random spot-checks summon the holder to pick walnuts from their own trellis within a day, so one operator cannot tend two groves at once. The grove fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real grove, another season of labor, another human, and twice the prior fee.
